findings.title: Broad data read + write = data manipulation risk
findings.description: Tools that can both read and write data could be manipulated to corrupt, overwrite, or delete information. Provided by: search_memories, create_memory, list_memory_labels, query_memories, get_guidance (data_read) + create_memory, create_connection, update_memory, update_connection, delete_memory, delete_connection (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Code execution + filesystem = unrestricted local access
findings.description: Tools that execute code AND access the filesystem can read/write any file the agent has permissions for, including SSH keys and credentials. Provided by: query_memories, dream (code_execute) + delete_memory, delete_connection (filesystem).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Credential access + data write = privilege persistence
findings.description: Tools that access credentials AND write data could persist stolen credentials or create backdoor accounts. Provided by: search_memories (credential_access) + create_memory, create_connection, update_memory, update_connection, delete_memory, delete_connection (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.recommendation: Validate all data before writing to agent memory. Implement integrity checks on persistent context. Log all memory modifications for audit.

findings.title: Trust exploitation pattern: authority impersonation
findings.description: Pattern in .smithery\index.cjs near line 4288: `representing`. This could enable a compromised agent to mislead users.
findings.recommendation: Implement output verification. Require human confirmation for high-impact actions. Mark agent-generated content as such.

findings.title: Rogue agent indicator detected
findings.description: Pattern in .smithery\index.cjs near line 17603: `Schedule(parentSubscription, scheduler, work, delay, repeat`. This could indicate self-modifying behavior, persistence mechanisms, or evasion capabilities.
findings.recommendation: Implement behavioral monitoring and kill switches. Ensure all agent actions are logged and auditable. Run in sandboxed environments with strict resource limits.

findings.title: Unpinned install source
findings.description: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` without a pinned version in run-inspector.sh at line 25. Without an exact version the next install silently picks up whatever is published, including a compromised release.
findings.recommendation: Pin an exact version (pkg@1.2.3, pkg==1.2.3) and prefer a lockfile or hash-checked requirements.

findings.title: Blast radius: HIGH — compromise of this server has broad impact
findings.description: If this MCP server is compromised, the blast radius is HIGH due to: arbitrary code execution, filesystem access, credential access, 12 tools (large attack surface), 95 critical findings. A single tool poisoning or supply chain attack could cascade across all connected systems.
findings.recommendation: Apply least-privilege to this server. Isolate it from other MCP servers. Implement kill switches and behavioral monitoring. Limit env vars to the minimum required.

tools.name: search_memories
tools.description: Hybrid keyword + semantic + fuzzy name search across the knowledge graph. "Ben Wicks" can find "Benjamin Weeks". Results include _score, _match and, for fuzzy hits, _matched (the stored name or alias that matched).

query.description: Search text to find in any property. Keyword mode matches any word, while semantic mode can surface close meanings and name variants.

depth.description: Relationship depth to include, 0 to 5, defaults to 1

order_by.description: Sort order such as created_at DESC, name ASC

limit.description: Maximum results to return, 1 to 200, defaults to 10

since_date.description: ISO date string to filter memories created after this date (e.g., "2024-01-01" or "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z")

search_mode.description: Search mode: hybrid (default), keyword-only, semantic-only, fuzzy name matching, or exact (case-insensitive equality on name/aliases/email: use before creating a memory).

fuzzy_threshold.description: Fuzzy name-match cut-off for misspelled or misheard names

similarity_threshold.description: Semantic similarity threshold, 0 to 1 inclusive, defaults to 0.4.

include_archived.description: Include memories with status "archived" (excluded by default).

tools.name: create_memory
tools.description: Create a new memory in the knowledge graph. Consider that the memory might already exist, so Search → Create → Connect (its important to try and connect memories)

label.description: Memory label: a plain identifier, Capitalised singular by convention (Person, Place, Organization, Project, Event, Topic, Object, Animal, Concept, Meeting, Decision…). Use list_memory_labels first for consistency; dream canonicalises lowercase labels.

properties.description: Information to store about this memory (use "name" as primary identifier, e.g. {name: "John Smith", age: 30, occupation: "Engineer"})

tools.name: create_connection
tools.description: Create a connection between two memories (its good to have connected memories)

type.description: Relationship type such as KNOWS, WORKS_ON, LIVES_IN, HAS_SKILL, PARTICIPATES_IN

tools.name: update_memory
tools.description: Update properties of an existing memory such as adding more detail or make a change when you find out something new

nodeId.description: ID of the memory to update

tools.name: update_connection
tools.description: Update properties of an existing connection between memories

type.description: Relationship type to identify which connection to update (e.g. WORKS_AT, KNOWS, MANAGES)

tools.name: delete_memory
tools.description: Delete a memory and all its connections (use with caution - this permanently removes the memory and all its connections)

nodeId.description: ID of the memory to delete

tools.name: delete_connection
tools.description: Delete a specific connection between two memories (use with caution - this permanently removes the relationship)

type.description: Exact relationship type to delete (e.g. WORKS_AT, KNOWS, MANAGES)

tools.name: list_memory_labels
tools.description: List all unique memory labels currently in use with their counts (useful for getting an overview of the knowledge graph)

include_archived.description: Include labels of archived memories (excluded by default).

tools.name: query_memories
tools.description: Run a read-only Cypher query and return up to 200 scrubbed rows.

params.description: Optional parameter map for the Cypher query.

tools.name: memory_stats
tools.description: Summarize node, relationship, label, embedding, and orphan counts for the graph.

tools.name: dream
tools.description: Deterministically relabel, merge duplicates, and refresh embeddings, with an optional dry run report.

dry_run.description: If true, report planned changes without writing them.

tools.name: get_guidance
tools.description: Get help on using the memory tools effectively

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
